# Caitlin Carney Tattoo: every page as text

> Caitlin Carney is a tattoo artist at True Colours Tattoo & Piercing Studio, 14 Guildhall Street, Preston, Lancashire, England. She tattoos portraits of people, pets and film and TV characters, Christian pieces, and script and lettering, in black and grey or colour. Walk-ins on Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays when she has a gap.

This is every page of caitlincarneytattoo.co.uk as plain text, for AI assistants and search tools, rewritten from the pages each time the site changes. The short version, with a link to each page, is https://caitlincarneytattoo.co.uk/llms.txt.

- Artist: Caitlin Carney. Before 2026 she tattooed as Caitlin O'Brien.
- Studio: True Colours Tattoo & Piercing Studio, 14 Guildhall Street, Preston PR1 3NU, next to the Guild Hall in Preston city centre. Phone: 01772 378565 (the studio).
- Days: at the studio Monday to Saturday. Walk-ins on Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays when she has a gap; ring the studio on the day to check.
- Main work: portraits (people, pets, characters from films and TV, and memorial portraits of someone who has died) and Christian pieces (crosses, scripture and bible verses, praying hands, rosaries, angels, portraits of Jesus and Mary). Also script and lettering, including a loved one's handwriting, and small pieces and flash. Black and grey or colour.
- Specialisms: realism portraits built up from clients' own photos (people, pets, film and TV characters), and Christian tattoos from an artist who shares the faith.
- The studio: True Colours is rated 4.9 on Google from over 1,300 reviews (November 2026).
- Every design is drawn up before the appointment and changed together until it's right, before the stencil goes on.
- Prices: small pieces and walk-ins from £70 (the studio minimum); script, names and dates from £70; a palm-sized portrait from £210; a half-day session £210; a full-day session, about six and a half hours, £400; cover-ups from £140. A £40 deposit holds a booking and comes off the final price.
- Booking: send the idea through the studio's booking form, https://www.truecolourstattoo.co.uk/quotation-booking-request, or as a message on Instagram.
- Instagram: @caitlincarneytattoo, https://www.instagram.com/caitlincarneytattoo/
- Clients come from Preston, from across Lancashire, and from around the North West of England.

#### Faith pieces from someone who shares it

Faith is a big part of my life. A cross, a verse, praying hands, Jesus or Mary: you're trusting it to someone who knows what it means to you.

#### Straight answers and clear prices

If a photo won't work, or a piece is too small to hold its detail, I'll tell you before you pay anything. Small pieces start from £70, and every quote is agreed up front.

### About me

I'm Caitlin Carney, a tattoo artist at True Colours in Preston. I've always loved drawing portraits more than anything, especially characters from films and TV shows, and that carries straight into my tattooing. And I love anything Christian: faith is a big part of my life.

Most of my clients come from Preston and around Lancashire, and a good few travel from across the North West. You'll find me at the studio on Guildhall Street, next to the Guild Hall in the city centre, Monday to Saturday.

Before 2026 I tattooed as Caitlin O'Brien, so you may have seen my work under that name.

[More about me](https://caitlincarneytattoo.co.uk/about/)

### Booking

- Send me the idea. A few lines, where on the body, rough size, and any reference pictures. Instagram messages or the studio's form both work.
- I come back with a quote. Usually within a few days. Bigger pieces are priced by the session.
- A £40 deposit holds your slot. It comes off the final price.
- We tattoo. I draw the design up before the day, and we make any changes together before the stencil goes on.

[Send a booking request](https://www.truecolourstattoo.co.uk/quotation-booking-request) [Message me on Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/caitlincarneytattoo/)

Walk-ins are welcome on Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays when I have a gap. Ring the studio on 01772 378565 on the day to check. [Prices and what to expect](https://caitlincarneytattoo.co.uk/prices/).

### Questions people ask

#### How much does a tattoo cost?

Small pieces start from £70. Larger custom work is priced by the session: £210 for a half day and £400 for a full day. The [prices page](https://caitlincarneytattoo.co.uk/prices/) has the detail. Send me the idea and I'll give you a clear price before you pay anything.

#### Do you do colour?

Yes. I work in black and grey and in colour. Tell me what you're picturing and I'll say which suits it.

#### Do you do cover-ups?

Sometimes, when the old tattoo suits it. Send a clear photo of it in daylight and tell me what you'd like instead, and I'll tell you straight whether I can work with it. Cover-ups start from £140.

#### Do you do memorial tattoos?

Yes. A portrait of someone you've lost, their handwriting from a card or a note, a name and a date, or a cross that carries them. The [portraits](https://caitlincarneytattoo.co.uk/portrait-tattoos/) and [script](https://caitlincarneytattoo.co.uk/script-tattoos/) pages cover how I work on them.

#### Can I just walk in?

On Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays, yes, for small pieces. Ring the studio first on 01772 378565 to check I have a gap that day. Custom work is always booked in advance.

#### Is there a deposit?

Yes, £40. It holds your appointment and comes off the final price. It's non-refundable if you cancel with less than a week's notice.

#### How old do I need to be?

Eighteen, with photo ID on the day. That's the law in the UK, with no exceptions for parental consent.

#### How do I look after a new tattoo?

I'll go through aftercare with you at the end of your session and send you home with written instructions. In short: keep it clean, keep it moisturised with a thin layer, and keep it out of the sun and out of baths and pools for two weeks.

#### Can I bring a friend?

One friend is fine. The studio is a working space, so big groups aren't.

## Portrait tattoos in Preston

Portraits are the work I love most. People, pets and characters from films and TV, built up from your own photos in black and grey or colour, at True Colours in Preston.

[Get a quote](https://www.truecolourstattoo.co.uk/quotation-booking-request) [Prices](https://caitlincarneytattoo.co.uk/prices/)

- Photo: Portrait tattoo of Frankenstein's monster, black and grey

### How I work

I've always loved drawing portraits more than anything, especially characters from films and TV shows, and that skill carries straight into my tattooing. If it's a family member or an animal, I need a high quality, professional-level photo to work from.

The photo decides everything. A portrait is only as good as its reference. Sharp, well lit, the face filling the frame, no heavy filters. Bring two or three and we'll pick the one with the best light. Old or small photos can still work, and I'll tell you honestly if one won't.

Faces need room. Eyes, teeth and hair need space to read clearly now and to stay clear as the tattoo ages. For a single face I suggest at least the size of your palm. Smaller than that, and detail turns to mush within a few years.

Black and grey or colour. Black and grey holds its detail for decades: soft greys and solid blacks, built up in layers over the session so they heal smooth. Colour brings a character to life. I do both, and I'll tell you which suits your photo.

#### Film and TV character portraits

The portraits I love most. Send me the character and the scene or still you have in mind. Film stills are usually sharp and well lit, which makes them good references.

#### Pet portrait tattoos

Dogs, cats, horses: fur, eyes, the tilt of a head. The same rules apply. A clear photo at their eye level, in daylight, not from above.

Where it goes. Flat, fleshy areas hold a portrait best: upper arm, forearm, thigh, calf, chest, shoulder blade. Fewer bends means less distortion when you move.

How long it takes. A palm-sized portrait is usually a half-day session. Larger pieces, or more than one face, take a full day or more than one session.

### Questions about portraits

#### How much does a portrait tattoo cost?

A palm-sized portrait starts from £210, which is a half-day session. Bigger pieces are £400 for a full day of about six and a half hours. Send me your photo and the size you have in mind and I'll quote before you pay anything.

#### Can you tattoo a portrait from an old or blurry photo?

Often, yes, if the face is clear enough to read. I can also combine two photos, say the eyes from one and the smile from another. If a photo won't work, I'll say so rather than guess.

#### Do you do colour portraits?

Yes. I work portraits in black and grey and in colour. Black and grey holds fine detail longest; colour is right for a lot of characters and some photos. We'll decide together from your reference.

#### Can you do a memorial portrait of someone I've lost?

Yes. Bring the best photo you have, and anything else that matters: their handwriting, a date, a line from a song. It's priced like any portrait, from £210, and there's no rush on these. If you're not ready for a long session, we start small and add to it later.

#### Does a portrait hurt more than other tattoos?

No more than any other tattoo in the same spot. Portraits take longer, so the session is longer. Eat beforehand, bring water, and we take breaks when you need them.

## Script and lettering tattoos in Preston

Script tattoos are words you want to keep for life: a quote, a line of a poem, a verse, a song lyric, a name, or someone's actual handwriting. I letter them cleanly so they still read in ten years, at True Colours in Preston.

[Get a quote](https://www.truecolourstattoo.co.uk/quotation-booking-request) [Prices](https://caitlincarneytattoo.co.uk/prices/)

- Photo: Watercolour flowers with the word Resilience in script, on the forearm

### How I work

Lettering has to survive. Thin lines spread a little as they age. I size letters so they still read in ten years: small script stays simple, and fine line script gets a bit more room between the letters.

The style follows the words. A poem might want a soft cursive. A date wants something upright. A lyric might want the lettering from the album. Bring examples you like and I'll draw it in your proportions, rather than pasting a font on.

#### Handwriting tattoos

A signature, a line from a card, a note someone left. These are the most meaningful pieces I do. Photograph the original flat in daylight and I'll keep it true to the hand that wrote it.

Where it goes. Along the collarbone, down the ribs, inside the forearm, along the spine. Words follow the lines of the body, so I draw it on you first and you check it in the mirror before the stencil.

Spelling. Checked three times, by both of us, before the needle goes anywhere near you.

### Questions about script tattoos

#### How much is a script tattoo?

A word or two starts from £70. A line or a short verse costs more, depending on length and where it goes. Longer poems are priced by the session, £210 for a half day. I'll quote before you pay anything.

#### How small can lettering go?

Small enough to still be readable in years, not just today. If your idea needs to grow a little to last, I'll tell you.

#### Can you do it in another language?

Yes. Bring the text written out correctly by someone who reads the language, and I'll copy it exactly. You check the stencil before we start.

## Christian tattoos in Preston

Christian tattoos are some of the most personal work I do, and faith is a big part of my own life. At True Colours in Preston I tattoo crosses, scripture and bible verses, praying hands, rosaries, angels, and portraits of Jesus and Mary, for people from across Lancashire.

[Get a quote](https://www.truecolourstattoo.co.uk/quotation-booking-request) [Prices](https://caitlincarneytattoo.co.uk/prices/)

- Photo: Mary in prayer beneath a gothic church window, fine line, upper arm

### How I work

Faith is a big part of my life. Tattooing Christian pieces means I can commit my work to my faith, help other Christians get good tattoos from someone who shares their experiences and values, and meet others who hold the same faith.

Scripture, word for word. Tell me the translation you read and the reference. I set the verse exactly as it's written, and we check it together before the stencil goes on.

Classic images, drawn for you. Praying hands holding your own rosary, a cross with a name and date, the Sacred Heart, Our Lady, an angel for someone you've lost. Reference pictures help, and I redraw rather than copy.

Portraits of Jesus and Mary. The same approach as my [portrait work](https://caitlincarneytattoo.co.uk/portrait-tattoos/): a clear reference, enough size for the face to read, in black and grey or colour.

Small and quiet works too. A small cross on the wrist, a single word, a fish, a dove. Not everything needs to be big to mean something.

Respect. I treat these designs with the same care you do, and I'll always show you the drawing before anything is final.

### Questions about faith tattoos

#### How much is a cross or scripture tattoo?

Small crosses and single words start from £70, and so does a short verse. Praying hands, rosaries and portraits are priced by the session: £210 for a half day, £400 for a full day. I'll quote before you pay anything.

#### Can you do a bible verse in the exact wording?

Yes. Tell me the translation and the chapter and verse. I'll show you the stencil before we begin, and you check every word.

#### Can a cross carry a name and date for someone I've lost?

Yes. A lot of the crosses I do are memorials. Bring the name and date, or their handwriting from a card, and I'll set it into the design.

## Walk-in and small tattoos in Preston

Walk-in tattoos are small pieces done the same day, no booking needed. I take them at True Colours in Preston city centre on Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays, when I have a gap between appointments. My flash designs are on my Instagram.

[Ring the studio: 01772 378565](tel:+441772378565) [Prices](https://caitlincarneytattoo.co.uk/prices/)

- Photo: Small black and grey butterfly tattoo on the arm

### How it works

Ring first. A quick call to the studio on 01772 378565 saves a wasted trip. If I have a gap, come down with your ID.

What counts as small. Up to about palm size, in simple linework or light shading: a name, a symbol, a small animal, a date, a tiny flower, matching pieces for friends.

Flash. Ready-drawn designs you can pick on the day. My flash is on Instagram: there's a highlight on my profile, and new sheets go up in posts and stories. Pick one, pick a spot, and you're usually done within the hour.

Your own small idea. Send it a day or two ahead on Instagram and I'll have it drawn up for when you arrive.

Bring. Photo ID, because you must be 18 and the studio checks. Eat beforehand. Wear something that gives easy access to the spot.

### Questions about walk-ins

#### How much is a small tattoo?

The studio minimum is £70, which covers most walk-in pieces. Anything bigger I'll price on the spot before we start.

#### Which days do you take walk-ins?

Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays are my walk-in days. I'm at the studio Monday to Saturday, but it always depends on gaps, so ring on the day.

#### Can two of us get matching tattoos as walk-ins?

Yes, if there's time. Ring ahead and say there are two of you.

## Prices and booking

Here's how I price work, so there are no surprises. Every quote is agreed before you pay anything.

### Prices

- Small pieces and walk-ins (studio minimum): from £70
- Script, names and dates: from £70
- Palm-sized portrait: from £210
- Half-day session: £210
- Full-day session, about six and a half hours: £400
- Cover-ups, priced from a photo of the old tattoo: from £140
- Deposit: £40, off the final price

Prices depend on size, detail and where on the body it goes, so these are starting points. Send me the idea and I'll give you a firm price. For a cover-up, send a clear daylight photo of the old tattoo first.

Deposits. The deposit is £40. It holds your appointment and comes off the final price. It's non-refundable if you cancel with less than a week's notice. Move your appointment with more notice than that and the deposit moves with it.

Paying. Cash or bank transfer, please.

Gift vouchers. Yes. True Colours sells studio-wide gift vouchers, so one can be spent with me or with any artist there. Ring or call into the studio to get one.

### How booking works

- Send me the idea. A few lines, where on the body, rough size, and any reference pictures. Instagram messages or the studio's form both work.
- I come back with a quote. Usually within a few days. Bigger pieces are priced by the session.
- A £40 deposit holds your slot. It comes off the final price.
- We tattoo. I draw the design up before the day, and we make any changes together before the stencil goes on.

[Send a booking request](https://www.truecolourstattoo.co.uk/quotation-booking-request) [Message me on Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/caitlincarneytattoo/)

### Before your appointment

- Eat a proper meal an hour or two before, and bring a drink and a snack for longer sessions.
- Sleep well the night before, and skip alcohol: it thins the blood and makes the tattoo harder to do.
- No sunburn on the area. I can't tattoo over it.
- Wear loose clothes that give easy access to the spot, and that you don't mind getting a little ink on.
- Bring photo ID. You must be 18, with no exceptions.
- Bring your reference pictures, or the card with the handwriting, even if you've already sent them.

---

Source: https://caitlincarneytattoo.co.uk/lancashire/

## Where my clients come from

I tattoo in Preston city centre, and people come from across Lancashire and the North West. Here's how to get to the studio from the places I see most, and where to park.

### The studio

True Colours is at 14 Guildhall Street, Preston PR1 3NU, next to the Guild Hall. It's about a ten-minute walk from Preston railway station and five minutes from the bus station.

Parking. There are plenty of public car parks nearby. The main one is the Fishergate Shopping Centre car park, about £4 for the day and a short walk from the studio.

Trains. Preston is on the West Coast Main Line, with direct trains from most of Lancashire, Manchester and Liverpool. [Open the studio in Google Maps](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=True+Colours+Tattoo+14+Guildhall+Street+Preston+PR1+3NU).

### Getting here

Rough times from the towns my clients travel from. Check the day's traffic and trains before you set off.

Leyland

About 15 minutes by car, under 10 by train.

Chorley

About 25 minutes by car, 15 by train.

Blackburn

About 30 minutes by car, 20 to 25 by train.

Lancaster

About 30 minutes by car, 15 to 20 by train.

Wigan

About 30 minutes by car, 15 to 20 by train.

Blackpool

About 40 minutes by car, 25 to 30 by train.

Southport

About 45 minutes by car. The train goes round by Wigan, so driving is easier.

Burnley

About 45 minutes by car, 50 by train.

Manchester

About 50 minutes by car, 45 by train.

Liverpool

About an hour by car, 50 minutes by train.

### Why people travel

Nobody drives an hour for a small walk-in, and nobody needs to. People travel for the work that takes planning: a [portrait](https://caitlincarneytattoo.co.uk/portrait-tattoos/) of someone you've lost, or of a character from a film, a [Christian piece](https://caitlincarneytattoo.co.uk/christian-tattoos/) with the verse set exactly, or [handwriting](https://caitlincarneytattoo.co.uk/script-tattoos/) from a card. If that's you, send me the idea first and we can do most of the planning by message before you make the trip.

If you're coming a long way for a full-day session, say so when you book and I'll try to start early.

Source: https://caitlincarneytattoo.co.uk/about/

## About me

I'm Caitlin Carney, a tattoo artist at True Colours in Preston, Lancashire. Portraits and Christian pieces are the work I love most.

### How I got here

I was always creative and loved drawing when I was young. I was good at it, and I knew I could have a job where that skill counted, so I'd do a great job and love it at the same time.

I started my apprenticeship in 2023.

The work I love most is portraits, especially characters from films and TV shows, and anything Christian. Faith is a big part of my life, and tattooing Christian pieces means I can commit my work to my faith and help other Christians get good tattoos from someone who shares their values.

I also do [script and lettering](https://caitlincarneytattoo.co.uk/script-tattoos/), memorial pieces, the odd cover-up, and [walk-ins](https://caitlincarneytattoo.co.uk/walk-in-tattoos/) on Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays. I work in black and grey and in colour.

### The studio

True Colours Tattoo & Piercing Studio is on Guildhall Street in Preston city centre, next to the Guild Hall. I haven't been at True Colours long, but the environment there as a working artist is incredible and the friendships are great. I was a customer before I worked there, and my experience then was brilliant.

Most of my clients come from Preston and around Lancashire: Chorley, Leyland, Blackburn, Blackpool and Lancaster. A good few travel from further across the North West for bigger pieces. There's a page on [getting here](https://caitlincarneytattoo.co.uk/lancashire/).

### My old name

Before 2026 I tattooed as Caitlin O'Brien. Same hands, same work, new name. If you had a piece from Caitlin O'Brien at True Colours, that was me, and I'd love to see how it's healed.

### Work with me
